candidates.name: claude/equalize_boost
candidates.description:
Edit: scale the DIRECT LETTER READOUT (the component of a w2 column that the tied letter rows read through post_ffn_norm and the final norm; a 9-dim subspace) by 0.5 for (a) the 8 letter-specific "leader suppressor" neurons of layer 22's MLP, model.layers.22.feed_forward.w2.weight columns C 1812, D 464, E 7357, F 6492, G 3344, H 397, I 2786, J 3310, and (b) 4 early-letter "booster" neurons: L22 column 2212 (A), L23 columns 1685 (A), 2595 (A), 1439 (B). The rest of each column is unchanged. 24,398 weights differ in bf16.
Mechanism: after head L22.H12 moves the chosen option to the answer position, the L22 MLP suppresses the currently leading letter through one neuron per letter (-3 to -4.6 logits when that letter leads). There is no such neuron for A or B, and A/B have boosters. Total suppression of a leader: A -1.2, B -2.2, C..J -4.1 to -5.6. That asymmetry makes the model over-pick early letters (practice: A..C predicted 249 vs 168 true out of 512). Halving the late-letter suppressors and the A/B boosters equalises it.
Evidence (paired, practice): screen256 DEV +2.34 (SE 1.35), +9/-3; dose-response for the suppressors alone: alpha 0.5 +1.56 (SE 0.95), alpha 0 +1.56 (SE 1.23) with more churn; adding layer 23's suppressors hurt (+1.17, SE 1.41). HOLDOUT 512 (never used for choices): parent 32.62 -> 33.98, +1.37 (SE 1.01), +17/-10. Side effect: the correct letter's log-probability falls (-0.13), because the suppressors also damp overconfidence.

candidates.name: ed_a/ed_a_qprimacy_L22L20
candidates.description:
Removes the option-ordinal ("primacy") query component from the answer-selecting attention layers L22 and L20.
Change: model.layers.22.self_attn.q_proj.weight and model.layers.20.self_attn.q_proj.weight, all 16 heads. For head h: W_h <- W_h - t t^T W_h (alpha = 1), where W_h = rows h*128:(h+1)*128 and t = normalize(q_norm.weight * v1_g). v1_g is PC1 of the slot-mean key vectors (k_norm outputs averaged over the tokens of options A..J, 120 DEV questions) of kv group g = h//4. Rank-1 per head, 2 tensors.
Mechanism: L22 is NoPE-like (q.k on recorded q_norm/k_norm reproduces the attention logits, residual var 0.3%). Option keys carry an ordinal position signal along v1 (slot means A -5.7, B -3.8, ..., J +0.3; split-half r .97). The answer-position query has a near-constant large component along v1 (about 32% of |q|), so every option-reading L22 head prefers early options by about 2.2 nats (A vs I). L20 (RoPE, but v1 sits in low-frequency pairs) has the same mechanism with an A-first preference of about 1 nat. Removing it flattens the letter prior: centred I goes from -2.1 to -0.6.
Evidence (paired edited - parent): DEV S1 (DEV[512:768], 256 q): +1.95 (SE 1.87), logp(correct) +0.186 (SE 0.060). HOLDOUT 512 practice questions (never used for any choice): +0.39 (SE 1.46), 29 w->r / 27 r->w, logp +0.197 (SE 0.055). The log-prob gain is robust, but the accuracy gain is not significant. A becomes under-picked (gold-A accuracy .43 -> .22).

candidates.name: claude/gate_wrapup_L20
candidates.description:
# gate_wrapup_L20: a gated "stop re-checking" neuron in layer 20

Edit: repurpose the quiet MLP neuron 5414 of layer 20 (model.layers.20.feed_forward w1 row, w3 row, w2 column; about 2,048 weights each).
- gate (w1 row) = commit direction - threshold x bias proxy. The commit direction is the mean-difference direction between
  residual states at points where the model has just stated its answer inside <think> and matched control points, read from recorded activations.
  The threshold is at the 99.8th percentile of all-token scores (s > 10.28), so it fires on about 0.2% of tokens.
- up (w3 row) = bias proxy (a direction with a near-constant projection, so the neuron's output is about gate-score minus threshold).
- down (w2 column) = (wrap-up word direction - reopen word direction) mapped back through the final norm (regularised inverse),
  scaled so that the estimated logit-difference shift at commit points is -9 (scale 0.400).
  Wrap-up words exclude </think> itself.
No training, no fitting beyond means and percentiles of recorded activations.

Mechanism measured (pass 3, read): at commit points that reopened, P(reopen) 0.81 -> 0.68 and P(close) 0.11 -> 0.24 (at target -3).
Control tokens are unchanged; the neuron fires (> 0.5) on 71% of commit points and 10% of controls.

Evidence (thinking mode, 3072-token cap, fixed seeds, paired original vs edited):
- DEV (32 practice questions, used for tuning): 37.5 -> 46.9 (+9.4, SE 6.9; +4/-1); cut share 0.53 -> 0.31; tokens -377.
- HOLDOUT A (32 fresh practice questions, untouched): 31.2 -> 34.4 (+3.1, SE 3.1; +1/-0); tokens -50.
- HOLDOUT B (32 fresh practice questions, untouched): 9.4 -> 18.8 (+9.4, SE 5.2; +3/-0); cut 0.81 -> 0.69; tokens -253.
- HOLDOUTS combined (64): +6.3 pp (SE about 3.0; +4/-0).
Where it helps: traces that state an answer and then re-check until the cap; it does nothing for traces that never commit.
Risk: on finished traces it shortens the thinking (same answers so far); one DEV loss (mmlupro_9424).

candidates.name: ed_a/ed_a_g5_churn_hence_L23
candidates.description:
